summary: At just 1.2 square miles with nearly 25,000 residents packed in at over 20,000 people per square mile, Maywood is one of the most densely populated cities in all of California — smaller than many college campuses yet functioning as a fully incorporated municipality wedged into the southeast Los Angeles basin. The terrain is dead flat, part of the broad alluvial plain of the Los Angeles River, which runs along the city's eastern edge, and the street grid is tight and unbroken, with small commercial corridors threading through residential blocks rather than separated by wide arterials or freeway buffers. With a home price-to-income ratio near 9.6× and a rent-to-income ratio consuming roughly 29% of the median household's gross pay, renting is the more realistic path for a household earning around $61,655; buying demands either substantial savings or dual incomes well above the local median. The economy leans heavily on small businesses, light manufacturing, and service-sector employment, with most workers commuting outward — the 710 and 5 freeways border the area, connecting to the massive logistics and industrial corridors of Vernon and Commerce immediately next door. Daily weather is remarkably consistent, averaging 76°F highs and 9.4 hours of sunshine year-round, which suits the outdoor, sidewalk-oriented rhythm of a place where nearly everything is within walking distance by sheer geographic compression. Maywood's defining reality is that extreme density on a tiny footprint creates a kind of urban village intensity — convenient and compact, but with housing costs that strain even moderate incomes.
